ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a six-membered ring structure, with a carbonyl C=O connected at the upper right; on the right side there is also an R substituent connected by one bond to a carbon on the ring; H is marked below, and there is B: as well as several curved arrows. Reasoning: As required, ignore all curved arrows. There are a total of 6 C-C bonds around the six-membered ring. Although the carbonyl C=O is drawn as a double bond, as one connection it is counted as 1 bond. The C-R substituent connection is counted as another 1 bond. The marked C-H bond involves hydrogen and is excluded; B: has no covalent bond drawn and is not counted. Therefore the total is 6 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: First ignore all curved arrows. Count the six C-C bonds around the six-membered ring as 6. Then add the carbonyl C=O connection as 1, even though it is drawn as a double bond. Add the C-R substituent bond as 1. Exclude the C-H bond to the labeled H and do not count anything for B: because no covalent bond is drawn to it. Total = 6 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: Build the heavy-atom graph from the image. The six ring carbons form a closed cycle, giving 6 heavy-atom edges. The carbonyl oxygen is connected to the carbonyl carbon by one C=O edge. The R group is connected to the lower-right ring carbon by one C-R edge. The explicit C-H edge is omitted because it involves hydrogen, and B: has no edge because only an arrow points from it. Therefore the graph has 6 + 1 + 1 = 8 non-hydrogen bonds.
